title: Salisbury Steak
subtitle: Seasoned beef patties in brown onion gravy
excerpt: Seasoned beef mince shaped into oval patties and simmered in a thick onion and mushroom gravy. A hearty American diner dish that costs very little and delivers a lot.
sourceNotes: Named after Dr J.H. Salisbury who promoted minced beef in the 1890s. A standard diner dish across America, often served with mashed potato.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the cooked patties in gravy. Thaw overnight and reheat covered on the hob over low heat.
recipe.batchNotes: Easy to double. Shape and freeze uncooked patties between layers of baking paper for up to 3 months.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Shape the patties up to a day ahead and refrigerate uncovered so a skin forms; this helps them hold shape when cooking.

content.text: Salisbury steak is a seasoned beef patty cooked in gravy. It is not a hamburger; the mix includes breadcrumbs and is shaped into an oval. The gravy is the key part; get it deep and brown.
Combine the beef, breadcrumbs, egg, Worcestershire sauce, mustard, onion powder, salt, and pepper in a large bowl. Mix until just combined. Do not overwork it.
Divide into 4 equal portions. Shape each into an oval patty about 2cm thick.
Heat the frying pan over medium-high heat with no fat. Brown the patties for 3 minutes per side until well coloured. Remove and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium. Melt the butter in the same pan. Cook the onion for 8 minutes until golden, stirring often.
Add the mushrooms. Cook for 5 minutes until they release their liquid and it evaporates.
Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables and stir for 1 minute. Pour in the hot stock and Worcestershire sauce, whisking to avoid lumps. Bring to a simmer.
Return the patties to the pan. Simmer gently for 12 minutes, turning once, until cooked through and the gravy is thick. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: The patties break up in the gravy.
items.cause: Too little binder or the mince was too lean.
items.fix: Use mince with more fat and add an extra egg next time. Brown them fully before adding to the gravy.

items.symptom: The gravy is pale and flat.
items.cause: The onions were not cooked long enough to colour.
items.fix: Cook the onions until properly golden before adding flour. The fond from browning the patties also adds colour.
Remove the patties and boil the gravy for 3 to 5 minutes until it thickens to your liking.
